study.question: After auxiliary gate transfer failed to beat self routing, can task-owned event routing benefit from learned interactions with each impression's feedback/match composition, and does keeping feedback identities matter beyond generic higher-order event interactions? The observed source limitation is that the inherited gate logit is a global linear function of 20 event feedback/match features; its coefficients do not themselves depend on history composition, although the downstream L1 normalization already does.
study.hypothesis: A target-matched feedback event can have different predictive value in histories where that feedback/match combination is rare versus common. A per-task bilinear interaction between each event and the masked within-example mean of the same input-only features can learn these differences without transferring auxiliary-task learned representations into click. History-conditioned routing should beat matched event-local bilinear routing; if feedback identity is consequential, this advantage should shrink when only the new route's feedback slots are collapsed. These are prospective hypotheses, not measured gains or a claim that auxiliary-label supervision is beneficial.

study.proposed_difference: For valid event i, form e_i in R20 from exposure plus the four overlapping historical feedback channels crossed with all/category/brand/both target-match indicators. In the history cell h=sum_valid(e)/max(valid_count,1); add r_it=e_i^T W_t h/sqrt(20) to task t gate logits before the inherited self multiplier/tanh. The local replacement uses r_it=e_i^T W_t e_i/sqrt(20). W has shape [4,20,20], zero initialized after the inherited reset. A second factor averages just the four feedback channels in the NEW route, preserving exposure and their sum; inherited static gate and evidence stay resolved. Both alternative logits execute in all cells. No current labels/actions, learned auxiliary donor, cross-example inputs, timestamps or new loss are introduced.

falsifiers: H_resolved fails to exceed L_resolved in click AUC: the specific history-conditioning benefit is unsupported under the frozen recipe. A gain against the smaller incumbent alone does not distinguish capacity from mechanism.

I<=0 or H_resolved fails to exceed H_collapsed: resolved feedback-identity complementarity is unsupported for the new route; no claim about utility of auxiliary-label supervision follows from either outcome.
Positive single-seed effects that fail authorized paired seed/user-cluster uncertainty checks remain provisional; exact reruns are reproducibility checks, not independent repetitions.

Nonfinite tensors/gradients, padding or sample-order dependence, nonzero empty-history correction, changes to inherited initialization outputs, cross-task gradients into the new W rows, or failure of click score-L1 preservation invalidate interpretation until corrected with all failed costs retained.
A null result tests this bilinear mean-composition implementation only. It does not refute richer task/context conditioning or full unified architectures.
alternative_explanations: Allocated capacity matches, but feature rank and gradient geometry differ: e^T W e observes only the symmetric matrix part and binary/match identities create further redundancies; e^T W h can identify directional interactions. This suite tests the concrete representation replacement, not a capacity-free theorem about conditioning.
Collapsing identities lowers effective feature rank and changes feature scale/correlation while preserving exposure and summed feedback slots. It is neither a union nor a shuffled-label control.
Inherited score normalization already couples events within a history; only the added learned dependence on history composition is varied.
Shared context embeddings, dense global clipping and optimization trajectories can couple losses indirectly; one frozen seed cannot establish significance or generalization beyond this dataset.

Gains may reflect extra task-specific parameters, richer deterministic match interactions, data-dependent regularization or easier optimization rather than feedback complementarity. The event-local and collapsed cells limit but do not remove all of these explanations.

Official offline historical feedback can be immature at impression time, and auxiliary labels are user/category/brand 24-hour matches rather than ad conversions; no point-in-time production or advertisement-specific conversion conclusion.
Multiple preceding validation-adapted rounds create selection uncertainty; unchanged single-pass training and same seed do not eliminate validation overfitting.

local_evidence_review.observation: Primary-owned selector AUC .6576086162 exceeded joint .6554607825; blocking auxiliary item gradients reached .6601633627, while restoring item gradient at .1 gave .6596625223. These comparisons motivated isolation, not a universal negative-transfer law.

Learned auxiliary residual transfer (.6592574965) and label-field sharing (.6592436764) did not beat the private-item parent (.6601638278). These are unsuccessful scientific branches with successful executions, not missing data or runtime failures. Wider alternatives remain unrefuted.

Target-matched evidence .6618104871 exceeded availability-only .6602926533; collapsing feedback identities was close at .6617253391. Event gate .6624770287 exceeded mean gate .6618218327, while event-collapsed .6624545972 was close. Matching and event resolution have stronger observed effects than identity; identity is consequently an uncertainty to test, not an established benefit.

Redistribution .6633488027 exceeded full .6626801586, scale-only .6617903610 and no click gate .6617449728 in one frozen seed. Preserve this operator while investigating a different source limitation. Coefficient-L1 mass is not pooled-vector norm.

After mass control, auxiliary donor AUCs .6630566462/.6630471075 still trailed self .6633139829/.6633488027. Live-versus-detached differences are small; no auxiliary superiority or significance. Self-live exactly reproduced the parent at the same seed and source, not independent repeated support. Latest knowledge declarations concerning potential auxiliary transfer did execute, but their complementarity prediction was not supported.
